- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated continuation; cap forecast rise to 3–5% below true peak.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5) and price shows no clear trend, model overfits noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.1 for 5+ days), model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% downward buffer to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; weight final 5–7 days of history 2x in smoothing to capture tail behavior.
- If sentiment is rising sharply (e.g., 0.2→0.5 in 3 days), model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven breakout.
